tags: why do dogs circle before lying down
script: Every night the ritual begins. Your dog turns in a slow circle, sometimes two or three, scratches at the bed, and only then finally flops down. It looks silly on a perfectly soft cushion, but this habit goes back to their wild ancestors. In tall grass or leaves, circling would flatten the area into a comfortable nest and push aside anything uncomfortable, like sticks or insects. It may also have helped them check the spot for danger and position their body so they could smell the wind and notice anything approaching. Curling up tightly afterward keeps vital organs protected and conserves body heat. Some dogs also circle to spread their scent from glands in their paws. For most dogs this is completely normal. The only time to pay attention is if the circling becomes frantic, or your dog seems unable to settle or appears to be in discomfort, since joint pain can make lying down awkward. Otherwise, just enjoy it, because it's a small piece of instinct playing out right on your living room floor.
